dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Quantas vezes o número 5 cabe dentro do 12 sem passar dele?
Tente dividir 12 por 5. O quociente será a sua parte inteira (m1) e o resto será o novo numerador (m2). O denominador (m3) permanece o mesmo.
O número 5 cabe duas vezes no 12 (5 + 5 = 10). Quanto sobra para chegar em 12?
Você tem 2 inteiros (10/5). Para chegar em 12/5, falta quanto? Preencha m1 com 2, m2 com o que sobrou e m3 com 5.
Lembre-se que cada unidade na reta está dividida em 5 partes iguais. Onde o número 2 se localiza?
Localize o número 2 na reta. A partir dele, conte duas das cinco pequenas marcações invisíveis para a direita.
Se cada marca vale 1/5, a segunda marca após o número 2 é o lugar correto.
Conte: 2, depois 2 e 1/5, e finalmente 2 e 2/5. O ponto deve ficar exatamente na segunda marca após o 2.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 5 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

componentes.papel: campo numérico da caixa de baixo da fração (denominador)
campo: numerador da parte fracionária do número misto ("-" quando não há)
campo: denominador da parte fracionária do número misto ("-" quando não há)
reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)
grupo com m1/m2/m3, exibido depois de Convert
botão "Convert": abre as caixas do número misto (m1, m2, m3) para reescrever a fração
campo numérico da caixa de cima da fração (numerador)
campo numérico: parte inteira do número misto

dicas.texto: The numerator tells how many individual pieces are being counted.
Find the total number of pieces Brandon gave away and enter that quantity in the top box.
Look in the problem for the number that describes all the pieces given to Brandon's friends.
Enter the total number of pieces given away in the upper fraction field.
The denominator describes the number of equal pieces in one whole.
Identify how many gum pieces are in one complete pack and place that number in the bottom box.
Use the pack size, not the total number of pieces Brandon gave away.
Enter the number of pieces contained in a single pack in the lower fraction field.
A fraction greater than one can be represented using whole groups and a remaining fractional part.
Compare the numerator with the denominator, then use the button that opens the mixed-number fields.
Because the total pieces exceed one pack, choose the control that ...s an improper fraction.
After checking that both fraction fields are filled, click the button labeled ....
A mixed number shows complete packs first and the leftover part of another pack second.
Divide the total pieces by the pieces in one pack; the quotient is the whole-number part and the remainder becomes the numerator of the fraction.
Use 5 as the divisor, record the complete groups, and keep the denominator equal to the original pack size.
Enter the quotient in m1, the remainder in m2, and the original denominator in m3.
Each unit on the line is divided into five equal parts because one pack contains five pieces.
Locate the second whole-number interval and use the fifth-part spacing within that interval.
The value is two complete units plus two of the five equal parts toward the next unit.
Place the point at the position corresponding to two and two-fifths, then submit that marked fraction value.
A correct solution should show the same value in the fraction representation and on the number line.
Review the numerator, denominator, mixed-number fields, and marked point before submitting.
Check that the point is two whole units and two fifths, and that the mixed-number fields agree with it.
When every field and the point are correct, click the button labeled ....

What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you.

Divide the total pieces by the pieces in one pack; the quotient is the whole-number part and the remainder becomes the numerator of the fraction.
Use 5 as the divisor, record the complete groups, and keep the denominator equal to the original pack size.
Enter the quotient in m1, the remainder in m2, and the original denominator in m3.

misconceptions.feedback: The denominator should remain the pack size. The leftover pieces go in the numerator, while the original number of pieces per pack stays in the denominator.

misconceptions.description: Aluno não completa a divisão total, parando no primeiro inteiro
misconceptions.feedback: You removed one complete pack but stopped too soon. After taking one group of five from twelve, there are still enough pieces for another complete pack.

misconceptions.description: Aluno arredonda o resultado da divisão para o próximo inteiro
misconceptions.feedback: Three complete packs would require more pieces than Brandon gave away. Count only the complete groups that fit within the total.

hints.message: Each unit on the line is divided into five equal parts because one pack contains five pieces.
Locate the second whole-number interval and use the fifth-part spacing within that interval.
The value is two complete units plus two of the five equal parts toward the next unit.
Place the point at the position corresponding to two and two-fifths, then submit that marked fraction value.

misconceptions.description: Aluno trata o numerador como a posição absoluta na reta, ignorando a escala da fração
misconceptions.feedback: The numerator is not an absolute position on the line. The denominator determines the size of each fifth-part step.

hints.message: A correct solution should show the same value in the fraction representation and on the number line.
Review the numerator, denominator, mixed-number fields, and marked point before submitting.
Check that the point is two whole units and two fifths, and that the mixed-number fields agree with it.
When every field and the point are correct, click the button labeled ....
